history.period: c. 6th-9th century (Gupta period to early medieval - dates vary by source)
history.summary: Adi Badri (Sri Sarasvati Udgam Tirath) is an ancient pilgrimage complex in the Shivalik foothills regarded as the origin point of the Sarasvati river. Tradition says Lord Vishnu resided here during the Satya, Treta and Dwapar yugas, and that Maharishi Ved Vyas composed the Mahabharata nearby (Bilaspur is said to be the corrupted form of 'Vyas Puri'). The site is a group of 16-17 ancient temples assigned by sources to the Gupta period (6th-9th century AD) and early medieval era, with Buddhist stupas and monasteries also found in ASI Shimla Circle excavations of 2003-04; the main temple is dedicated to Vishnu. The complex includes the Adi Narayan Mandir, Adi Kedarnath Mandir and Mantra Devi Mandir (INTACH built-heritage listing; Mantra Devi is sister row 350 - a distinct shrine in the same complex, not a duplicate). Not to be confused with the Sapta Badri Adi Badri temple near Karnaprayag in Uttarakhand. Festivals: International Saraswati Mahotsav (Jan, inaugurated 2025 by CM Nayab Singh Saini), Akha Teej Mela (Apr-May), and the Adi Badri-Kapal Mochan Kartik Purnima mela (Nov). Haryana is developing the site under its Morni-to-Kalesar tourism plan; an Adi Badri dam project on the Somb is also proposed nearby. CSV town 'Yamunanagar' corrected: the site is ~38 km northwest of Yamunanagar city, in Bilaspur tehsil. Coordinates are from a government forest-clearance report (30 deg 26'56"N, 77 deg 20'45"E).

name: Adi Badri Dham (Sri Sarasvati Udgam Tirath)
town_description: Adi Badri is a village and tirtha site in Bilaspur tehsil of Yamunanagar district, Haryana, in the Shivalik foothills about 38 km northwest of Yamunanagar city. It is regarded in tradition as the spot where the Sarasvati river emerges from the hills.
